what: What was the unexpended balance of each Lunenburg capital project article at 30 June 1998?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds the Town Accountant's capital project fund schedule, article by article, from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1998 annual town report prints no such schedule: the only capital project figure is the CAPITAL PROJECT FUND column of the combined balance sheet (PDF page 43, TOTAL LIABILITIES/FUND EQUITY $302,415.48). Its text was searched on all 97 pages with text for `capital project`, `project fund`, `unexpended` and `article` beside a balance, and returned only that column and prose about building projects (p10, p17, p27) (sources/data/report-tables/1998/). — closes: the Town Accountant's FY1998 capital projects fund ledger (balances by article at 30 June 1998).

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in 1998?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1998 annual town report prints neither: its text was searched on all 97 pages with text for salary schedule, classification plan, Schedule A, step, and grade beside a dollar figure, and returned only school pay lanes printed per teacher in the GRADE column of the school wage list (p87-93, e.g. `M+75 MAX`), which are labels, not rates (sources/data/report-tables/1998/). — closes: the Personnel Bylaw Schedule A (salary schedule and classification plan) in force for FY1999, from the Town Clerk or the Personnel Board.

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1998, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fees from the 2010 report. The 1998 annual town report prints no Inspector of Weights & Measures report: its text was searched for weights, sealer and sealing and returned only the appointment (p9), the receipts line SEALING FEES $796.00 (p44), the appropriation line (p49), the omnibus line WEIGHTS/MEASURES (p79) and the inspector's wage line (p96) (sources/data/report-tables/1998/). — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 1998 annual report to the Division of Standards.

what: What did each item of Lunenburg's FY1999 capital plan cost?
why: `capital-plans` holds item-by-item costs. The 1998 annual town report gives the FY1999 plan only as a total in prose (`The FY'99 Capital Plan was approved in FY'98 for $458,659.00`, p11) and as warrant articles that name items without an amount per item: Articles 27 ($17,100), 28 ($127,000: dump truck, cruiser, voting equipment, generator, computers), 29 ($128,000: ambulance, sander) and 30 ($98,000: handicap access, fire suppression, fire alarms) of the May 9, 1998 ATM (p78). Its text was searched for capital plan, capital expenditure and capital improvement (sources/data/report-tables/1998/). — closes: the Capital Planning Committee's FY1999 Capital Plan as presented to the May 9, 1998 Annual Town Meeting.

what: How much of Lunenburg's debt at 30 June 1998 sat inside the debt limit, and how much outside it?
why: `outstanding-debt` reads this from the five-year outstanding-debt summary the FY2011-FY2025 reports print. The 1998 annual town report prints its bonded indebtedness issue by issue (PDF page 62), a repayment schedule (p61) and the LONG TERM DEBT account group on the balance sheet (p43), but no summary by purpose and no debt-limit split: its text was searched for debt limit, outstanding debt, long-term debt, inside/outside and exempt, and returned only the balance-sheet lines and tax exemptions. — closes: the Town's FY1998 Statement of Indebtedness as filed with the Division of Local Services.
